# Agent Switcher

Create, manage, and switch your own **agents** in DeepSeek Harness — from a
sidebar **Agents** tab, from the composer, and from a `custom_agent` tool the
model can call to author a specialist and run it as a subagent.

An agent here is a DSH **agent preset**: a declared composition of tools,
prompt sections, skills, and policies. The plugin adds a user registry on top of
the shipped preset rows.

## Agent files

Your agents live under **`~/.config/dsh/agents`** (on Windows
`C:\Users\<you>\.config\dsh\agents`) as one Markdown file per agent:
**`<id>.md`**, in the same shape opencode uses.

```markdown
---
name: Reviewer
description: Reviews changes and reports findings.
template: standard
mode: subagent
model: deepseek-chat
reasoning: high
tags: [review, typescript]
pinned: true
tools:
  bash: false
allow: [custom_agent]
handoffs: [fixer]
defaults:
  cwd: C:\work
  prompt: Review the staged diff.
---

You review software changes. Cite files and keep findings terse.
```

- **Body** — the agent's instructions; it becomes the preset's persona prefix.
- **`template`** — which shipped/custom preset supplies the tool composition
  (`standard` by default, or `ptc`, `minimal`, `cordis`, or another of yours).
- **`tools`** — opencode-style `tool: false` flags, mapped to DSH tools and
  applied with a per-agent tool restriction. The panel edits them as checkboxes.
- **`model` / `reasoning`** — applied to this agent's **delegations**
  (`agentOptions`); an interactive session still uses its own model route.
- **`mode`** — preserved for round-tripping with opencode.
- **`tags`, `pinned`** — panel filtering and ordering.
- **`allow`** — capabilities the agent opts into. Today the only value is
  `custom_agent`: it lets this agent create and start further subagents. Root
  agents always may.
- **`handoffs`** — agent ids this specialist may hand work onward to; the list is
  appended to a delegation prompt as a hint.
- **`defaults`** — working directory and starter prompt for a new session.
- A file without frontmatter is imported as a prompt-only agent named after the
  file.

Every write keeps the previous revision under **`.history/<id>/<timestamp>.md`**
inside the store, so an edit can be undone from the panel.

On host start every file is registered with the harness preset registry, so it
joins the roster that New Session, the preset picker, and the composer chip
read. Creating, editing, importing, and deleting in the panel register or
unregister it live.

## opencode import

**Import from opencode (N)** in the panel reads
`~/.config/opencode/agents` (and `~/.config/opencode/agent`), copies every
`*.md` file that is not already in your store, and registers it. The files are
copied unchanged, so the same file can live in both tools.

## The Agents panel

The sidebar tab is a small workspace for the roster:

- **Search and filter.** The box matches name, id, tag, or description; clicking
  a tag chip narrows the list to that tag. Pinned agents sort first.
- **Edit anything.** The edit form exposes identity, instructions, template,
  model, mode, reasoning effort, tool checkboxes, tags, pinning, allow
  delegation, declared handoffs, and session defaults — the same fields the
  Markdown frontmatter holds.
- **Try an agent.** *Try* opens a new session on that agent with an optional
  starter prompt, so a test is one click instead of a session-and-cleanup
  ritual. It starts a real session; the reply appears there.
- **History, duplicate, restore.** Each write snapshots the previous file.
  *History* lists revisions and restores one; *Duplicate* makes a variant with a
  fresh id and name.
- **Share.** *Copy* puts the whole Markdown agent on the clipboard, *Export*
  downloads it, and the import box accepts pasted Markdown. Dragging a `.md`
  file onto the panel imports it too.

## Custom agents from the model

The agent can build a specialist itself. The host registers a **`custom_agent`**
tool with three actions:

| Action | What it does |
|---|---|
| `list` | Returns the saved custom agents, with tags and declared handoffs. |
| `create` | Writes a new `<id>.md` into the same store the panel uses and registers it. Takes `name`, `instructions`, `description`, an optional `id`, `template`, `tags`, `model`, `reasoning`, and `handoffs`. |
| `delegate` | Starts that agent as a subagent on its own preset, with a prompt you supply. Returns the child's session id immediately. |

So "make me a code-review agent and have it review this" works in one turn: the
model calls `create`, then `delegate`, and continues working while the child
runs. The delegation uses a fresh-context provider that advertises
`agentPreset` (the in-process `spawn`; fork-style providers inherit the parent
and are skipped), re-reads and mounts the agent file first, passes the agent's
`model` and `reasoning` in `agentOptions`, and records the custom agent's id in
the child's `agentPreset` header.

**Delegation is gated.** A root agent may always call `custom_agent`; one of
your agents may only when its frontmatter says `allow: [custom_agent]` (the
panel's *Allow delegation* switch), so a child cannot recursively spawn agents
unless you asked for that.

The child starts with an empty context, so a delegation prompt must carry every
fact it needs. A system-prompt section also nudges the model to use
`custom_agent` when the user asks for a specialist or when a saved agent fits
better than doing the work inline.

## Surfaces

| Where | What it does |
|---|---|
| Sidebar → **Agents** | Search, tag-filter, pin, edit every field, try, duplicate, view history, copy/export/import, delete, and start a session on an agent. |
| Composer chip | Shows the current agent, opens the roster, and switches the session. `Tab` / `Shift+Tab` cycles while the composer is empty. |
| `custom_agent` tool | Lets the model author an agent and run it as a subagent (`list`, `create`, `delegate`), gated by `allow`. |
| `/agent` | Lists the roster; `/agent <id>` switches the session. `/agents` is a listing alias. |
| `/agent-create`, `/agent-update`, `/agent-duplicate`, `/agent-pin`, `/agent-restore`, `/agent-import`, `/agent-import-text`, `/agent-delete` | The command channel the panel uses first, so authoring works even if a custom Web route's POST is unavailable. |

## Theme

Every color, surface, border, and shadow comes from the harness theme tokens the
shipped components use — `--dsw-alias-*`, `--dsw-specific-menu`,
`--dsw-shadow-lv3` — including the primary button's fill, hover, and
foreground pair and the composer trigger's exact geometry. Light, dark, and
third-party skins (such as dsh-claude-style) therefore restyle the chip and the
panel with the rest of the app; there are no hard-coded brand colors, no
`color-mix` tints, and native controls inherit the app's `color-scheme`.

The stylesheet is rendered as a `<style>` element **inside each surface's React
tree**, not appended to `<head>`: the live shell may replace or drop head
styles during theme and HMR passes, while an element in the component tree is
re-created with the surface and lands in the same document (or shadow root).

The dropdown uses the same **MenuSurface material** as the composer's model
picker: `--dsw-specific-menu` (the translucent menu fill) over
`--dsw-menu-backdrop-filter` (`blur(40px) saturate(150%)`), no border, with the
elevation shadow. Where a token is absent, the menu falls back to the base
theme's fill for the current scheme (`#ffffff` light, `#43454a73` dark), so it
looks like the model menu even in a surface that lost the theme variables.

The panel and the composer menu can render outside the element that carries the
theme's custom properties (a portal or the shell's panel surface). Where a token
is absent, every surface falls back to a small local palette built with CSS
`light-dark()`, which follows the root's `color-scheme`, so the panel and menu
stay opaque and legible in both schemes instead of collapsing to transparent.

## Install

Published on npm as **`dsh-agent-switcher`**.

In the DeepSeek Harness app, open **Settings → Plugins → Add** and enter
`dsh-agent-switcher`. With the plugin-manager tool:

```
plugin_manager  action: install_bundle  target: dsh-agent-switcher
```

From a local checkout instead:

```
plugin_manager  action: install_bundle  target: C:\Users\<you>\Documents\Code\dsh-agent-switcher
```

or link it with the harness CLI:

```powershell
dsh plugin --profile desktop add link:C:/Users/<you>/Documents/Code/dsh-agent-switcher
```

The npm package installs a copy; a linked checkout reflects edits under `lib/`.
The host half loads on the next host start, the browser half on the next page
refresh.

> **Careful with a linked checkout.** The plugin manager installs an absolute
> path as a `link:`, and **uninstalling that bundle deletes the checkout's
> contents**. Keep a copy (or publish first) before removing a link install; an
> npm install is an ordinary copy and is safe to remove.

## Files

| Path | Role |
|---|---|
| `lib/index.js` | Host: store, revision history, runtime preset registration, `custom_agent` tool, the HTTP routes and slash commands. |
| `lib/client.js` | Browser: composer chip, sidebar row, Agents panel (search, settings, history, try), locale dictionaries. Hand-written; only `react` is external. |
| `cordis.patch.yml` | Inserts the host row into the profile. |
| `locale/en.json`, `locale/zh.json` | Plugin-manager display metadata. |
| `icon.svg` | Original plugin icon. |

## HTTP face (same-origin)

- `GET /agent-switcher-2/agents` — roster (agents with metadata, presets, catalog, importable opencode files).
- `POST /agent-switcher-2/agents` — create one agent from its fields.
- `GET /agent-switcher-2/agent?id=<id>` — one agent with its parsed record and instructions.
- `POST /agent-switcher-2/update?id=<id>` — update fields (snapshots the previous file).
- `POST /agent-switcher-2/duplicate?id=<id>` — copy under a fresh id.
- `POST /agent-switcher-2/pin?id=<id>` — `{ pinned }`.
- `GET /agent-switcher-2/history?id=<id>` — saved revisions.
- `POST /agent-switcher-2/restore?id=<id>` — `{ stamp }`.
- `GET /agent-switcher-2/export?id=<id>` — the Markdown file as a download.
- `POST /agent-switcher-2/import` — no body imports every opencode agent; `{ text }` imports one pasted agent.
- `POST /agent-switcher-2/delete?id=<id>` — removes one of your agents.

Requests pass the harness browser-trust fence (`connection.requestRejection`).
Creating, importing, and deleting in the panel go through the slash-command
channel first (`/agent-create`, `/agent-import`, `/agent-delete`), which rides
the harness's authenticated Remote transport; the HTTP routes are the fallback.

## Updating

The browser half reloads with a page refresh. The host half loads a plugin
module generation per plugin-manager apply: re-installing the bundle, or
toggling it off and on with `plugin_manager set_bundle` (same profile), unloads
the old generation and loads the new one, which re-registers the tool, the
commands, and the route without restarting the app. If a route from an older
build ever stays occupied (`webserver: duplicate prefix route`), one application
restart clears it — the route is owned by the plugin's effect, so it unregisters
on unload. Diagnostics are appended to `~/.config/dsh/agents/.route.log`
(`route registered`, `tool custom_agent registered`, `loaded N agent(s)`,
`loaded … failed`, and one line per rejected request).

## Known limitations

- **Deleting an agent does not rewrite history.** Sessions that already ran it
  keep their retained revision; a later resume of such a session needs the
  definition to exist again (the registry rejects a missing preset).
- **Switching mid-session changes the tool catalog and prompt** at the next
  message. That is the point, but it invalidates the prompt-prefix cache for
  that conversation.
- **A switch during a running turn** applies to the next step; the in-flight
  request keeps the composition it was assembled under. There is no
  "continue this conversation as X": the registry locks a session's preset once
  it has run a turn, so the safe path is a new session (what *Try* does).
- **The template is read when the agent is created or loaded.** A later change
  to a built-in preset does not reach agents already stored from it; recreate
  or change their file to pick it up.
- **The panel edits fields, not the composition.** Identity, instructions,
  settings, and metadata are editable there; the plugin list inside `template`
  still comes from the referenced preset (the harness-native Creator mode
  remains the path for bundle-declared presets).
- **`model` and `reasoning` apply to delegations, not interactive sessions.**
  An interactive session uses its own model route; these fields ride
  `agentOptions` when `custom_agent` starts a child.
- **Delegation needs a fresh-context provider.** `custom_agent delegate` uses
  the first provider that advertises `agentPreset` without inheriting the parent
  context (the shipped `spawn`). A profile with only fork-style providers cannot
  run a model-authored agent; the tool reports that instead of silently falling
  back to the parent's preset.

# Changelog

## 0.5.0 — 2026-10-20

Everything the panel showed before is still there; this release makes an agent
something you can actually tune and test.

- **Real per-agent settings.** The edit form now covers the fields the file
  already supported: model, mode (`primary` / `subagent` / `all`), reasoning
  effort, per-tool enable/disable checkboxes, declared handoffs, an
  **Allow delegation** switch, tags, pinning, a default working directory, and a
  starter prompt for new sessions.
- **History and restore.** Every write keeps the previous file as
  `.history/<id>/<timestamp>.md`. The panel lists revisions and restores one;
  duplicating an agent is a single action.
- **Search, tags, pinning, and sorting.** A filter box matches name, id, tag, or
  description; tag chips filter the list; pinned agents sort first; each card
  shows its model, mode, and revision count.
- **Try-it playground.** Each card can start a throwaway session on that agent
  with an optional prompt, so testing no longer means creating a session,
  switching the chip, typing, and cleaning up.
- **Share and import.** Copy an agent as Markdown, download its `.md`, or import
  one by pasting text or dropping a file on the panel; the opencode import from
  0.3.0 is unchanged.
- **Scoped delegation.** `custom_agent` is now gated: a root agent may create and
  delegate, while one of your agents must opt in with `allow: [custom_agent]` in
  its frontmatter. Delegations pass the agent's model and reasoning effort in
  `agentOptions`, and declared `handoffs` are appended to the child's prompt.
- **Richer tool surface.** `custom_agent` gained `tags`, `model`, `reasoning`,
  and `handoffs` on `create`, and `list` now prints tags and handoffs.

## 0.4.0 — 2026-10-19

- **The model can author and use custom agents.** A `custom_agent` tool is
  registered with `list`, `create`, and `delegate` actions: the model writes a
  specialist (name, description, instructions, template), saves it to the same
  store as the panel, then starts it as a subagent on its preset. The built-in
  `subagent` tool only accepts statically configured presets, so this is the
  first path from a model-authored agent to a running child.
- **A prompt-section nudge** tells the model to reach for `custom_agent` when a
  specialist fits, instead of doing everything in the parent session.
- **Fresh-context providers only.** Delegation picks a provider that advertises
  `agentPreset` and does not inherit the parent context (`spawn` by default), so
  the child really runs the chosen composition.
- **Re-registered per delegation.** The agent file is re-read and mounted just
  before the child starts, so a hand-edited file runs as edited.

## 0.3.0 — 2026-10-18

First public release.

- **Agents are opencode-style Markdown files.** One `<id>.md` per agent under
  `~/.config/dsh/agents`, with `name`, `description`, `template`, `mode`,
  `model`, and `tools` frontmatter and the instructions as the body.
- **Import from opencode.** The panel copies every `*.md` agent from
  `~/.config/opencode/agents` (and `…/agent`) without rewriting it, registers it,
  and maps `tools: { x: false }` flags onto DSH tool restrictions.
- **Composer chip + sidebar Agents tab.** Create, import, delete, and start a
  session on any agent; `Tab`/`Shift+Tab` cycles while the composer is empty.
- **Authored through the command channel first** (`/agent-create`,
  `/agent-import`, `/agent-delete`), with same-origin routes as the fallback.
- **Theme-matched UI.** The chip and panel use harness tokens; the roster menu
  uses the same `MenuSurface` material as the model picker (translucent fill,
  `blur(40px) saturate(150%)`), with scheme-aware fallbacks where a token is
  absent.
- **Boot diagnostics** in `~/.config/dsh/agents/.route.log`.
